question: Can successful self-timed MLE programs finish sooner under sharing while yielding less useful output, and can admission improve final search quality under equal resources?
evidence_now: 18812:2chronological programs,8executions,work/quality reduction under co-location; candidate-time ratios0.9909931255242036/0.7988482912036062. Not allocation speedup, significance, causal mediation or E2E benefit.

sources.title: Semantic-Aware Scheduling for GPU Clusters with Large Language Models (SchedMate)
sources.overlap: Uses source/history/log semantics and training-throughput interference monitoring. Reading code or avoiding slowdown is not our novelty.
sources.comparison_needed: A faithful cheap interference-aware/semantic baseline, not just fixed GPU assignment; no claim of beating SchedMate from current data.

sources.title: HyperSched: Dynamic Resource Reallocation for Model Development on a Deadline
sources.overlap: Already optimizes best trained model by a fixed deadline and resource budget. Assumes intermediate progress, checkpoint/restore and common scaling properties; do not claim quality-aware resource allocation as new.
sources.difference_to_test: Opaque generated programs adapt their own work to wall clocks; no scheduler-controlled epoch interface. This distinction alone is not a new algorithm.

sources.title: Prediction-based GPU sharing for distributed training (TensorShare)
sources.scope_read: Primary author-hosted indexed abstract/introduction and footnote only, not full paper
sources.overlap: Predicts sharing-induced completion-time increase and constrains its ratio; footnote includes customized stopping conditions.
sources.difference_to_test: Our successful self-timed outputs show candidate duration can decrease along with quality. This warns against treating runtime-ratio compliance as quality preservation, not a reproduction or refutation of TensorShare.

sources.title: DeepSeek Elastic Compute (DSec)
sources.overlap: Overcommit and isolation of latency-sensitive agent sandboxes already exist, including CPU interference protection and separated CPU/GPU function execution.
sources.difference_to_test: Not a new sandbox-isolation system; our current measurement concerns completed MLE predictions and their learned work, not only latency SLOs.

sources.title: AgBench: Agentic AI Benchmarks for Personal AI Devices
sources.overlap: Already reports concurrency versus success/goodput tradeoffs, including local model context errors and timeout effects.
sources.difference_to_test: Our fixed-code replay removes model generation and gives valid predictions in every case; quality can change without an execution-error flag. Not claiming concurrency harming success is new.

sources.title: Scheduling Contract Algorithms on Multiple Processors
sources.overlap: Anytime/contract algorithms and time-quality scheduling are longstanding ideas. Self-timed output-quality tradeoffs are not generally new.
sources.difference_to_test: Would require a practical mechanism exploiting nonstationary generated-program behavior beyond classical resource/time allocation; current results do not establish this.

decision: Finish18807 final-score comparison and18819 chronological rank test first. Do not equate novel phrasing, a faster completion counter or local mechanism evidence with a publishable method. Do not restore multifidelity, timer rewriting or base training.
